title: The generalized continuum hypothesis in the constructible universe
summary: Count constructible levels, place subsets below the next cardinal using condensation, and prove GCH with the power sets and cardinals computed inside L.
abstract: The constructible universe admits far fewer subsets than the full power-set operation might suggest. We count definitions with finite parameters and prove that every infinite constructible level has the same size as its ordinal index. Condensation then puts each subset of an infinite cardinal below its successor stage when every set is constructible. Counting that stage proves the generalized continuum hypothesis from the axiom of constructibility. Running the argument inside L gives its internal GCH theorem. We distinguish the constructible power set and successor cardinal from their ambient counterparts, which need not have the same sizes.
